standard_prerequisites: Context span 1848-1917: the construction - k algebraic closure of a finite field, A = k[x,y], C = V(x) with enumerated closed points, auxiliary curves C_i, the Claim producing irreducible Z_n with {p_n} = Z_n cap (C cup C_1 cup ... cup C_n) via Cartier divisors and torsion Picard group of an affine curve, then S generated by the f_n with Z_n = V(f_n) and B = S^{-1}A, with the analysis of which maximal ideals survive (infinitely many from A, plus xB) yielding local rings of dimensions 1 and 2
Universally catenary rings: Algebra, lemma-localization-catenary and Morphisms, lemma-ubiquity-uc
core_obligations: The construction of B is given in the context span; the counted proof only has to add universal catenarity
B is universally catenary by Algebra, lemma-localization-catenary (localization of a catenary quotient of a polynomial ring) together with Morphisms, lemma-ubiquity-uc
Hence B is a Jacobson, universally catenary Noetherian domain whose maximal ideals m_1 (from A, dim 1) and m_2 = xB (dim 2) give dim B_m1 = 1 and dim B_m2 = 2
proof_roadmap: Take the constructed B from the context span
Conclude universal catenarity via the two named lemmas
Read off the two maximal ideals with local dimensions 1 and 2 from the spectrum analysis
